# Verify every landing and publish it to origin

## Intent

A change that landed on the hub is not finished: it may have broken the
main branch, and origin does not have it yet. nightshift runs the
workspace's health command on every landed commit and on every commit
origin brings in, repairs a broken main branch once and reverts the landing
when the repair does not help, and pushes the default branch to origin only
after the health command passed. A work item is `done` only then, and the
person is asked only where nightshift cannot go on by itself: a main branch
it could not make healthy, and an origin that refuses or has diverged.

## Goals

- **A landing that breaks the main branch is dealt with.** After every
  landing the health command runs on the landed commit. A failure makes
  the workspace `red`, starts one repair, and, when that does not make the
  branch healthy, reverts the landing.
- **Only verified work reaches origin.** The default branch is pushed to
  origin after the health command passed, and an item is `done` only when
  origin has the commit.
- **What origin brings in is verified too.** A sync that fast-forwards the
  default branch runs the health command on the new tip before anything
  lands.
- **Only what nightshift cannot settle reaches the person.** A main branch
  that stays unhealthy is a `main_red` decision; a refused push, a
  diverged origin and a sync that keeps failing are an `origin` decision.
  Each has one option, and the person is told when the workspace turns
  `red` or `held`.
- **It survives a restart.** A health run, a repair, a revert and a push
  that a stop interrupted are continued at the next start from what was
  stored, without a second repair and without a second revert.

## Non-goals

This package is the eighth of ten written from
`docs/prd/02-drive-work-items-through-the-hub.md`. Of this package's
neighbourhood, these belong to the others:

repair of a commit origin brought in.

## Background

Packages 01 to 07 leave an item in `verifying` when the hub landed its
change: the change's `landed.sha` is on the workspace's default branch on
the hub, and nowhere else. Nothing has run on that commit, and origin does
not have it.

What this package uses of Parley, as its `docs/api.md` states at commit
`7eabfb9`:

- A **land** moves only the hub's branch. Origin gets it through `POST
  …/branches/{name}/push`, which pushes the branch's head, whatever it is:
  the route takes no commit.
- A **revert** (`POST …/changes/{number}/revert`) builds, on the head of
  the target branch, one commit per landed commit of the original, each
  undoing it, and opens an ordinary change from the branch
  `revert/<number>`. Policy judges that change like any other; it lands
  through `POST …/land`. The caller of the revert is the creator of its
  version, so an approval of it counts only from another credential: the
  approver token.
- A **sync** (`POST …/sync`) answers one entry per branch of origin with
  `result`, `local_sha` (the hub's head after the sync) and `origin_sha`.
- A check result is reported per version with `PUT
  …/changes/{number}/checks/{name}`; a report replaces the earlier one
  whole.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: this
package adds no command and no route; what it does is read through the
inbox and the item commands of package 03.

### After a landing

When a change landed, nightshift runs the workspace's health command on a
clone of the workspace at the landed commit. Exit code 0 within the timeout
is healthy: the item is `publishing` (see *Publishing to origin*).

Any other exit code, or the timeout, makes the workspace `red`. While a
workspace is `red`, nightshift lands nothing else in it and pushes nothing
to origin: other items go on up to `landing` and wait there. Then:

1. **Fix forward.** nightshift starts one repair: an implementer session in a
   new fork, with the health command's last 200 lines of output, the
   landed change and the item's package. Its change is gated, reviewed and
   landed as any other, ahead of everything else and although the
   workspace is `red`. When it landed, the health command runs again;
   healthy makes the workspace `green` and both changes go on to
   `publishing`.
2. **Revert.** When the repair's session failed twice, its review ended in
   disagreement, or the health command still fails after it landed,
   nightshift asks the hub to revert the repair's change, when it landed,
   and then the item's change. On each reverting change it reports its
   three checks as `passed`, with the summary `revert after failed health
   command on <commit>`, and lands it. When the hub answers that a
   reverting change needs an approval, an `approval` decision goes to
   `Action`, listed before every other decision. After the reverts the
   health command runs again. Healthy makes the workspace `green`; the
   item returns to `awaiting_approval` with a `plan` decision that carries
   the failure's output.
3. **Still unhealthy.** When the health command fails after the revert,
   or a revert cannot be built or landed, the workspace stays `red` and a
   decision of kind `main_red` goes to `Action` with the output and the
   commits tried; its only option is `resume`, which the person chooses once
   the branch is repaired by hand and which runs the health command once
   more, staying `red` on a failure.

Each of the three steps writes an `Unread` entry to the item's thread.

Repair sessions start even when the workspace's daily limit is reached,
and are counted.

The thread entries of this package:

| Kind | Text | Unread |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | `health command passed on <commit>` | no |
| `health_failed` | `health command exited <N> on <commit>` or `health command timed out on <commit>` | no |
| `repair` | `workspace <slug> is red; repair started for change <n>` | yes |
| `revert` | `repair did not help (<reason>); reverting change <n>` with ` and change <m>` for a landed repair | yes |
| `workspace_green` | `workspace <slug> is green again` | no |
| `push` | `push of <branch> to origin: <result or error type>` | no |
| `published` | `change <n> is on origin as <commit>; <N> tokens spent` | yes |

The step *Still unhealthy* is marked by the entry the `main_red` decision
writes when it opens.

### Publishing to origin

When the health command passed on a landed commit, nightshift asks the hub
to push the workspace's default branch to origin. What the hub answers
decides:

- **pushed**, or origin already has the commit: the item is `done`, the
  fork is left to expire, and the thread gets an `Unread` entry with the
  change, the commit and the tokens spent.
- **origin has commits the hub lacks**: nightshift syncs, with the results
  below, and pushes again.
- **origin refused the push**, or the workspace's origin credential is
  missing or not accepted: the workspace is `held` and a decision of kind
  `origin` goes to `Action` with origin's reason; its only option is
  `retry`.
- **origin could not be reached**, or the push timed out: it is tried again
  after 1 minute, at most 5 times, then handled as a refused push.

**A sync from origin**, which nightshift runs before every landing and after
a push that origin's branch was ahead of, has one of these results for the
default branch:

- `up_to_date` or `ahead`: nothing more happens.
- `fast_forward`: origin brought commits. nightshift runs the health command
  on the new tip before it lands anything. A failure makes the workspace
  `red` with no item to blame: a `main_red` decision goes to `Action` in
  the workspace's thread.
- `diverged`: the workspace is `held` and an `origin` decision goes to
  `Action`, naming both heads; its only option is `retry`, which the person
  chooses once the two branches are reconciled by hand.
- the sync fails: it is tried again after 1 minute, at most 5 times, then
  handled as a refused push.

An `origin` decision answered with `retry` makes nightshift sync and push
again; the workspace is `green` when both succeed, and the decision opens
again with the new reason when they do not.

**Telling the person.** When a workspace turns `red` or `held`, nightshift
calls the notification command of package 03 with the event
`workspace_red` or `workspace_held`, the workspace, the item where there is
one, and the thread's URL path.

**New, added by this package to the Go packages of others** (nothing of

- **`(*impl.Service).UsePackageOf(ctx, item, of)`** in `internal/impl`

**How a repair runs.** A repair is a work item: a linked item of the kind
`defect`, created from the item whose landing failed, given that item's
package, the repair class and the repair mark, handed the health command's
output as a finding, and moved to `ready`. Packages 06 and 07 then
implement it as a rework in a fork of its own, gate, review and land it as
any item. When it reaches `verifying`, this package runs the health
command on its landed commit. A repair ends without having helped when the
repair item waits on any decision but an `approval`, or is abandoned.

### End-to-end flows

**A healthy landing is published.** Item 12's change landed. `nightshiftd`
clones the workspace at the landed commit and runs the health command,
which exits 0; the item is `publishing`. It asks the hub to push the
default branch; the hub answers `pushed`; the item is `done` and its thread
is in `Unread` with the change, the commit and the tokens spent.

**A landing that breaks the main branch.** Item 12 lands; the health
command exits 1. The workspace is `red`, nothing is pushed to origin, and
item 13, ready to land, waits. The repair lands and the health command
fails again. nightshift reverts both changes, the health command exits 0,
the repair item is abandoned,
the workspace is `green`, item 13 lands and is published, and item 12 is
back in `Action` with a `plan` decision carrying the failure's output.
Origin never held item 12's commit as the head of its branch.

**Origin refuses, and the person retries.** Item 14 is `publishing`; the
hub answers the push `422 origin_rejected` with origin's reason. The
workspace is `held`, the notification command receives `workspace_held`,
and an `origin` decision with the reason is in `Action`. The person fixes
the branch rule on the forge and answers `retry`. nightshift syncs, pushes,
the hub answers `pushed`, the workspace is `green` and item 14 is `done`.

## Design Decisions

From the source PRD, by its numbers:

- **11. A landed commit is pushed to origin after the health command
  passed, and `done` means it is on origin.** The owner decided it.
- **12. nightshift syncs from origin before each landing; only a
  divergence or a refused push reaches the person.** The owner decided it.
- **13. On a revert nightshift reports its own checks as passed and asks
  the person only where policy requires an approval.** The owner decided
  it.
- **21. Fix forward once and then revert; one health command per
  workspace.** Kept from PRD 01.
- **26. Repairs start although the daily limit is reached.** Chosen there.
- **28. A diverged origin has the one option `retry`.** Chosen there.
- **41. The health command runs as the session user.** Chosen there;
  `RunHealth` of package 02 with the identity of package 04 does it.

Chosen here:

1. **Two Go packages: `internal/health` (the health command after a
   landing, `red`, repair, revert, `main_red`) and `internal/publish` (the
   push, the sync's results, `origin`, `held`).** Why: the ownership the
   ten packages agreed on.
2. **A repair is a work item of its own: a linked `defect` item of the
   item whose landing failed, with that item's package.** Why: packages 06
   and 07 implement, gate, review and land items and nothing else
   (`Rework`, `SetClass` and `SetRepair` take an item), and a pause of the
   workspace then holds the repair as the source PRD asks. The item whose
   landing failed stays `verifying`; "both changes go on to `publishing`"
   is both items moving there. This replaces an earlier draft of this
   package, in which the repair belonged to the failed item.
3. **One incident is stored per failed health command, with its phase
   (`repairing`, `reverting`, `main_red`, `closed`), the output, the
   commits tried and the changes it opened.** Why: a step function is
   called again after a pause or a restart and must go on where it was.
4. **A health command that could not be run (the clone failed, the hub is
   unreachable, the command could not be started) decides nothing: the
   step ends and is called again.** Why: the source PRD makes a workspace
   `red` for an exit code or the timeout, and a failed fetch says nothing
   about the branch.
5. **While a workspace is `red` for another item, an item in `verifying`
   waits, and is then verified on the head of the default branch, not on
   its own landed commit.** Why: its own commit holds the broken change
   without the repair or the revert, and would fail for the other item's
   fault.
6. **A repair ends, and the landing is reverted, when the repair item
   waits on any decision but an `approval` (`session_failed`,
   `review_disagreement`, `session_limit`, `blocked`, `conflict`) or is
   abandoned; this package closes that decision and abandons the repair
   item.** Why: the source PRD names a session that failed twice and a
   review that ended in disagreement, and both reach this package as
   decisions packages 04 and 06 open by themselves; one more round for
   the others is not "one repair". The decision is open for at most one
   pass of the scheduler, and its notification is sent: accepted, since
   suppressing it would mean changing packages 04 and 06.
7. **The repair's change is reverted before the item's, and the item's
   revert is asked only when the repair's has landed.** Why: the hub
   builds a revert on the target's head, and the repair sits on top of the
   item's change.
8. **`409 already_reverted` is taken as the reverting change it names.**
   Why: a daemon stopped between the hub's answer and its own store asks
   again at the next start.
9. **"A revert cannot be built or landed" is every other refusal of the
   revert (`revert_conflict`, `nothing_to_land`, `target_not_found`, any
   other error answer) and a land of a reverting change that is refused,
   an `approval` answered `reject` or `abandon` among them. A land answered
   `failed` is not asked again.**
10. **The summary's `<commit>` is the item's landed commit, on both
    reverting changes; the three checks are reported on version 1 of the
    reverting change before its land is asked.**
11. **"Listed before every other decision" is a member `urgent` of a
    decision: `GET /api/v1/decisions` answers the urgent open decisions
    first, then the others, each group oldest first.** This package adds
    `Urgent` and `SetUrgent` to `internal/inbox`, and marks the decision
    package 07's `OpenApproval` returns. Why: package 03 orders decisions
    by their age alone, and package 07 leaves the listing to this package.
12. **A `main_red` decision answered `resume` runs the health command on
    the head of the default branch. Healthy: the workspace is `green`, and
    the item goes to `awaiting_approval` with the `plan` decision when its
    change's revert landed, else to `publishing`. Unhealthy: a new
    `main_red` decision opens with the new output.** Why: the source PRD
    says what `resume` runs and not what follows; the branch the person
    repaired either still holds the item's change or does not, and a `red`
    workspace with nothing in `Action` would wait for nobody.
13. **The `main_red` decision of an item is in the item's thread; the one
    after a `fast_forward` is in the workspace's thread. An `origin`
    decision for a refused push is in the thread of the item whose push it
    was; one for a sync's result is in the workspace's thread.** Why: an
    item with an open decision names it in `waiting_on`, and the source
    PRD puts what has no item to blame in the workspace's thread.
14. **A workspace has at most one open `origin` decision and one open
    `main_red` decision.** Why: one push serves every item, and a second
    question about the same branch says nothing new.
15. **The push is asked only while the workspace is `green`, no item of
    it is `verifying` and no health run on a fast-forwarded tip is
    pending.** Why: the hub pushes the branch's head, whatever it is, so
    a push while a later landing is unverified would publish unverified
    work.
16. **One push, and after a `non_fast_forward` one sync and one more push,
    per call of an item's step; an item still not on origin is tried again
    at the next call.** Why: a loop over an origin that keeps moving needs
    a bound.
17. **Refused: `origin_rejected`, `origin_unauthenticated`,
    `origin_forbidden`, `origin_not_found`, and every error answer of the
    push this document does not name. Tried again: `origin_unreachable`,
    `upstream_error` and `origin_timeout`.** A push the hub itself could
    not be asked for (the hub unreachable, the worker token not accepted)
    is neither and is not counted.
18. **"At most 5 times" is 5 further tries: the sixth failure in a row is
    handled as a refused push.** The count is kept per workspace in the
    store and starts again at any other answer.
19. **A sync that fails is tried again by this package, on a timer of its
    own; a failure package 07 hands over while such a try is pending is
    not counted.** Why: package 07's landing step is called every second,
    and the source PRD counts tries a minute apart.
20. **A sync that reports the default branch with another result (`reset`,
    `name_conflict`), or not at all, is a failed sync with the reason
    `sync reported <result>`; `created` is as `up_to_date`.**
21. **The fork of a `done` item is neither deleted nor extended.** Why:
    "left to expire".
22. **The tokens spent are the input, cache-creation and output tokens of
    every session of the item, a repair's among them.** Why: package 04's
    count, cache reads excluded.
23. **An answer to a decision of this package for an item that is paused
    takes effect at the resume.** Why: the source PRD's rule for every
    decision of a paused item; a decision in the workspace's thread is
    carried out at once.
24. **No event of its own.** The entries, decisions and state changes this
    package writes append `thread.updated`, `decision.*` and
    `item.updated` through package 03; the workspace's state setter
    appends none (package 02).
25. **The intervals (1 minute between tries, 5 tries) are parameters with
    these defaults, not configuration keys.** Why: the source PRD does not
    call them configured.
26. **A `retry` that does not succeed opens the `origin` decision again at
    once, without tries a minute apart.** Why: the person is there and has
    just said that origin is in order; five more minutes tell them less
    than the new reason does.
27. **The commit of the `published` entry is the commit the item's change
    landed as.** Why: after a repair the pushed head is another commit,
    and the entry is about the item's change.
28. **The repair item gets its package through a new function of
    package 06's `internal/impl`, `UsePackageOf`.** Why: building a fork,
    a change, a rework, a gate and a review a second time in this package
    would copy package 06; one function that points an item at another
    item's package lets its steps do all of it.
29. **After a revert the repair item, when it had landed, is moved to
    `awaiting_approval` and abandoned at once.** Why: `verifying` allows
    only `publishing` and `awaiting_approval`, and a reverted repair is
    neither published nor planned again.
30. **A reverted item whose package was imported gets no `plan` decision:
    it is moved to `awaiting_approval` with an unread `revert` entry that
    says so.** Why: package 05 keeps no text of an imported package and
    refuses `Reopen` for it; the person abandons the item and imports a
    corrected package. Reported as an open point.
31. **This package's own syncs go through package 07's `SyncOrigin`.**
    Why: one reader of the default branch's result.

## Verified External API

Parley's REST API, read in `docs/api.md` of `agent-fox-dev/parley` at
commit `7eabfb9`:

- `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/revert`, scope
  `changes:write`, the owner of `{slug}`: optional body `title`, `intent`,
  `draft`, `auto_land`, `session_id`; `201` with the new change (its
  `number`, `version`, `reverts` the original's number), opened from the
  branch `revert/<number>` into the original's target; `409
  change_not_landed`, `409 already_reverted` with
  `error.details.reverted_by`, `400 nothing_to_land`, `409
  revert_conflict` with `error.details.conflict`, `400 target_not_found`.
  A refusal leaves no branch and no change.
- `GET …/changes/{number}`: `state` (`draft`, `open`, `landed`,
  `abandoned`), `version`, `landed` (`null` until landed: `sha`, `at`,
  `by`, `land_id`, `commits`), `reverts`, `reverted_by`.
- `PUT …/changes/{number}/checks/{name}`, scope `checks:write`: `status`
  `pending|passed|failed`, `version`, `summary` of at most 2,000
  characters; `200` with the check; one result per version and name.
- `POST …/changes/{number}/land`, scope `changes:write`: optional
  `expected_version`; `200` with the attempt `landed` (`landed_sha`),
  `202` still `running`, `409 land_conflict`, `409 policy_blocked` (the
  attempt's `blocked.status` `pending` or `blocked`, with
  `requirements`), `409 version_mismatch`, `503 land_failed`.
- `POST …/branches/{name}/push`, scope `workspaces:write`: `200`
  `{branch, sha, remote, remote_url, result}` with `result` `pushed`,
  `forced` or `up_to_date`; `409 non_fast_forward`, `422
  origin_rejected`, `502 origin_unauthenticated`, `502 origin_forbidden`,
  `502 origin_not_found`, `502 origin_unreachable`, `502 upstream_error`,
  `504 origin_timeout`, `404 branch_not_found`, `400 fork_has_no_origin`.
  A push that fails changes nothing on origin.
- `POST …/sync`, scope `workspaces:write`: `200` with the workspace
  object plus `branches`, each `{name, result, local_sha, origin_sha}`,
  `result` one of `created`, `up_to_date`, `fast_forward`, `ahead`,
  `diverged`, `reset`, `name_conflict`; for `diverged` `local_sha` is the
  hub's head and `origin_sha` origin's; `400 sync_disabled`, `502
  upstream_error`, `500 internal`.
- The workspace object's `default_branch` and `head_sha`.

Packages 05, 06 and 07, read as drafts with `specr` on 2026-11-28: the
functions of *What this package uses of packages 05, 06 and 07*, with the
signatures given there. Not verified, because this package adds them:
`UsePackageOf` and `SetUrgent`.

## Glossary

- **health command**: the command a workspace configures that must exit 0
  on the default branch.
- **landed commit**: the commit a change landed as on the hub's default
  branch (`landed.sha` of the change).
- **incident**: one failed health command and everything nightshift did
  about it, until the workspace is `green` again.
- **repair item**: the linked work item that is given a failed health
  command's output and whose change is to make the branch healthy.
- **reverting change**: the change the hub opens to undo a landed one.
- **tip**: the head of the default branch after a sync moved it.
- **green, red, held**: the stored state of a workspace (package 02).
- **origin**: the repository on a forge that a Parley workspace was cloned
  from and is pushed to.
- **urgent**: a decision the inbox lists before the others.
- **hub, worker token, approver token**: as package 01 defines them.
- **step function, repair class**: as package 04 defines them.
- **change, version, check, land, sync**: as Parley defines them
  (`docs/api.md`).

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: The health command after a landing

**Rationale:** A change that passed its gate and its review can still break the main branch once it sits on top of everything else; only a run on the landed commit shows it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of an item in `verifying` whose workspace is `green` and which belongs to no incident, THE nightshiftd SHALL read the item's change (`change.Service.Get` of package 05 for its number, the hub client's `Change` for its `landed.sha`), run the workspace's health command on a clone of the workspace at the landed commit through `workspace.Service.RunHealth` with a tail of 200 lines, and, when the command exits 0 within the workspace's health timeout, append the entry `health` with the text `health command passed on <commit>` to the item's thread and move the item to `publishing`
   → `RunHealth` was called once, with the workspace's slug, the change's `landed.sha` and 200; the item is `publishing`; the workspace is still `green`; no incident is stored; no notification was sent
   Check: integration
   - setup: a health service over a copy of the store template with the real item service and inbox, the fake hub holding change 7 of item 12 landed as commit C, a stub of package 05's `change.Service.Get` answering `Record{Workspace: 'demo', Change: 7}` for item 12, and a stub in place of `workspace.Service` that records `RunHealth` and `SetState`
   ```
   new file internal/health/verify_test.go, fixtures in internal/health/helpers_test.go: stub.RunHealth returns {ExitCode: 0}; err = svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert err == nil; assert stub.healthCalls == [('demo', C, 200)]; assert items.Get(12).State == 'publishing'; assert the thread's entries hold {kind: 'health', text: 'health command passed on ' + C}; assert stub.state('demo') == 'green'; assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert notifier.events is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the health command run on an item's landed commit exits with a code other than 0, or does not end within the workspace's health timeout, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL set the workspace's state to `red` with `workspace.Service.SetState`, store an incident for the item in the phase `repairing` with the commit and the last 200 lines of the command's output, append the entry `health_failed` to the item's thread, call `Notify` of `internal/notify` with the event `workspace_red`, and leave the item `verifying`
   → the workspace's state is `red`; the item is still `verifying`; the incident holds the landed commit and at most 200 lines of output; the entry's text is `health command exited <N> on <commit>` or `health command timed out on <commit>`; exactly one notification was sent for the incident, with `event: workspace_red`, the workspace, the item's number and the item thread's URL path
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixtures of the passing case, with a recording notifier
   ```
   in internal/health/verify_test.go, a table over stub results {ExitCode 3 with 250 lines of tail -> entry 'health command exited 3 on C', TimedOut -> 'health command timed out on C'}: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert stub.state('demo') == 'red'; assert items.Get(12).State == 'verifying'; inc = svc.Incident('demo'); assert inc.Phase == 'repairing' and inc.Item == 12 and inc.Commit == C and len(inc.Output) <= 200; assert the entry text; assert notifier.events == [{Event: 'workspace_red', Workspace: 'demo', Item: 12, Thread: the item thread's path}]; call VerifyStep again; assert still one notification and one health_failed entry
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the item's change cannot be read (package 05 holds no record, the hub does not answer), the change is not landed, or `RunHealth` returns an error instead of a result (the clone failed, the hub is not available, the command could not be started), THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL decide nothing about the workspace and return the error from the step, so that the scheduler calls the step again
   → the step returns a non-nil error that names the cause; the workspace's state, the item's state and the item's thread are as before the call; no incident is stored and no notification is sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/health/verify_test.go, a table over {the fake hub answers the change read 502, the change's state is 'open' with landed null, stub.RunHealth returns an error 'cannot clone demo: …'}: err = svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert err != nil; assert stub.setStateCalls is empty; assert items.Get(12).State == 'verifying'; assert the thread has no entry of this package; assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert notifier.events is empty; then with the cause removed assert VerifyStep moves the item to 'publishing'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHILE a workspace is `red` and an item of it that is `verifying` is neither the item nor the repair item of the workspace's open incident, THE nightshiftd SHALL run no health command for that item and leave it `verifying`, and, at the first call of its step after the workspace is `green` again, run its health command on the head of the default branch (`head_sha` of the hub's workspace object) instead of its own landed commit
   → no call of `RunHealth` for the item while the workspace is `red`; the first call afterwards carries the hub's `head_sha`; a result of that run is handled as REQ-1.1 and REQ-1.2 say, with that commit
   Check: unit
   - setup: items 12 and 13 of 'demo' both `verifying`; an open incident of item 12; the fake hub's `head_sha` of 'demo' is H, item 13's landed commit is D
   ```
   in internal/health/verify_test.go: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item13) three times; assert no RunHealth call for D or H and items.Get(13).State == 'verifying'; close the incident as REQ-2.3 does (workspace green); stub.RunHealth returns {ExitCode: 0}; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item13); assert the last health call == ('demo', H, 200); assert items.Get(13).State == 'publishing'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any incident, keep in the store its phase, the output of each failed health command, every commit a health command ran on with its result, the number of its repair item and the numbers of the reverting changes it opened, and continue the incident from that record when the step of its item or of its repair item is called after a pause or after a restart of nightshiftd, creating no second repair item and asking the hub for no second revert of a change
   Check: integration
   - setup: a store file in a temporary directory, opened, used, closed and opened again with a new health service
   - setup: the incident of item 12 stored in the phase `reverting` with the repair item 13, whose change 9 is reverted by change 10, which has landed
   ```
   new file internal/health/revert_test.go: reopen the store; svc2.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert items.List('demo') holds no item beside 12 and its repair item 13; assert the fake hub saw no POST …/changes/9/revert; assert it saw exactly one POST …/changes/7/revert; assert svc2.Incident('demo').Phase == 'reverting' and its output and commits tried equal those stored before the restart
   ```

### REQ-2: Fix forward: one repair

**Rationale:** Most breakages are small, and a fix on top keeps the work that landed; one attempt bounds what a broken main branch may cost.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an incident of an item is in the phase `repairing` and has no repair item, THE nightshiftd SHALL create one repair item with the item service's `CreateLinked(ctx, <the item>, 'defect', <text>)`, the text naming the landed change and the commit; give it the package of the item it repairs with `(*impl.Service).UsePackageOf` (new in package 06's `internal/impl`, added by this package); ask for its sessions in the repair class with `SetClass(ctx, repair, sched.ClassRepair)`; mark it with `land.Service.SetRepair(ctx, repair, true)`; hand it one finding of the source `health` whose `Output` is the last 200 lines of the health command's output with `Rework`; move it from `new` to `ready`; and append once the entry `repair` with the text `workspace <slug> is red; repair started for change <n>` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, marking it unread
   → the incident stores the repair item's number before anything else is asked of it; the repair item is `ready`, a child of the item, of the kind `defect`; `Rework` received exactly one finding `{Source: 'health', Text: 'health command failed on <commit> after change <ref> landed', Output: <the tail>}`; a later call of the step for the same incident creates no second item, and repeats only the calls the record does not show as done; the thread holds exactly one `repair` entry and it is marked unread; the hub saw no revert request
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixtures of REQ-1.2 with recording stubs of package 06's `Rework`, `SetClass` and `UsePackageOf` and of package 07's `SetRepair`
   ```
   new file internal/health/repair_test.go: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12) with the failing health stub; inc = svc.Incident('demo'); r = inc.Repair; assert items.Get(r).State == 'ready' and its parent == 12 and its kind == 'defect'; assert impl.calls == [UsePackageOf(r, 12), SetClass(r, sched.ClassRepair), Rework(r, [{Source: 'health', Text: 'health command failed on ' + C + ' after change demo#7 landed', Output: the tail}])]; assert lander.calls == [SetRepair(r, true)]; make impl.Rework fail once in a second run of the case: the first step returns the error, the second calls Rework again and creates no second item; assert count(entries of kind 'repair' in item 12's thread) == 1 and the thread is unread; assert the fake hub saw no revert request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of a repair item in `verifying`, which packages 06 and 07 implemented, gated, reviewed and landed as any item although the workspace is `red`, THE nightshiftd SHALL read the commit the repair item's change landed as, run the health command on it through `RunHealth` with a tail of 200 lines, and add the commit and its result to the incident's commits tried
   → `RunHealth` is called with the slug, the `landed.sha` of the repair item's change and 200; the workspace is `red` until the result is handled; a call of the step of the item whose landing failed, while the repair item is not yet `verifying` and waits on no decision, changes nothing and returns nil
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/health/repair_test.go: walk the repair item r to 'verifying' with its change 9 landed as R on the fake hub; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12) first: assert nil, no health call, nothing changed; stub.RunHealth for R returns {ExitCode: 0}; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, r); assert the health call == ('demo', R, 200); assert stub.setStateCalls == ['red', 'green']; assert items.Get(12).State == 'publishing' and items.Get(r).State == 'publishing'; assert lander.calls ends with SetRepair(r, false); assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert item 12's thread holds 'health command passed on ' + R and 'workspace demo is green again'; assert the fake hub saw no revert request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN the health command exits 0 within the health timeout on the commit a repair item's change landed as, THE nightshiftd SHALL set the workspace's state to `green`, close the incident, remove the repair mark with `SetRepair(ctx, repair, false)`, append the entries `health` and `workspace_green` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, and move that item and the repair item to `publishing`
   → the workspace's state is `green`; both items are `publishing`; the incident's phase is `closed`; the hub saw no revert request; the `workspace_green` entry's text is `workspace <slug> is green again`
   Check: same as REQ-2.2
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the repair item of an incident in the phase `repairing` waits on a decision of a kind other than `approval` (`session_failed`, `review_disagreement`, `session_limit`, `blocked` or `conflict`), or is `abandoned`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL end the repair: close that decision with the inbox's `Close` and the reason `repair ended; the landing is reverted`, abandon the repair item with the item service's `Abandon` where it is not abandoned already, and go on to the revert of REQ-3.1 with the decision's kind as the reason
   → the repair item is `abandoned` and has no open decision; no second repair item is created; the incident's phase is `reverting` with the reason `session failed twice` for `session_failed`, `review disagreement` for `review_disagreement`, and `repair stopped: <kind>` or `repair abandoned` otherwise; a repair item that waits on an `approval` decision is left alone and the incident stays `repairing`
   Check: integration
   - setup: the decision kinds of packages 04, 06 and 07 declared in the test's inbox by name, with one option each
   ```
   in internal/health/repair_test.go, a table over the repair item r {in 'implementing' with an open session_failed decision -> reason 'session failed twice'; in 'reviewing' with review_disagreement -> 'review disagreement'; in 'implementing' with blocked -> 'repair stopped: blocked'; abandoned by the person -> 'repair abandoned'; in 'landing' with an open approval decision -> untouched}: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); for the first four assert inbox.OpenDecisions(r) is empty, the closed decision's reason == 'repair ended; the landing is reverted', items.Get(r).State == 'abandoned', inc.Phase == 'reverting' and inc.Reason; for the last assert the decision is still open, r is 'landing' and inc.Phase == 'repairing'
   ```

### REQ-3: Revert, and a main branch that stays unhealthy

**Rationale:** A repair that did not help must not be followed by another: taking the landing back is the one step that is known to have been healthy before.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a repair ended as REQ-2.4 says, or the health command exits with a code other than 0 or times out on the commit the repair item's change landed as, THE nightshiftd SHALL move the incident to the phase `reverting`, append once the entry `revert` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, marking it unread, and ask the hub with `POST …/changes/{number}/revert` to revert the repair item's change where it landed, and the item's change once the repair's reverting change has landed or where the repair's change did not land
   → the entry's text is `repair did not help (<reason>); reverting change <n>`, with ` and change <m>` for a landed repair, the reason one of those of REQ-2.4, `health command exited <N>` or `health command timed out`; a repair's change that did not land is not reverted; the revert of the item's change is not asked before the land of the repair's reverting change was answered `landed`; an answer `409 already_reverted` is taken as the change `error.details.reverted_by` names and no second revert is asked
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fake hub extended with the revert route: a landed change gets a reverting change with `reverts` set, a second request answers 409 already_reverted with `reverted_by`
   - setup: a recording stub of package 07's `LandChange`, `OpenApproval` and `OnApprovalAnswered`
   ```
   in internal/health/revert_test.go, a table over {the repair ended with 'session failed twice' -> requests [revert 7], entry '… (session failed twice); reverting change 7'; the repair ended with 'review disagreement' -> [revert 7]; the repair item landed as R and health exits 2 on R -> [revert 9, then revert 7 only after LandChange answered 'landed' for the reverting change of 9], entry '… (health command exited 2); reverting change 9 and change 7'}: drive svc.VerifyStep of item 12 and of the repair item until both return; assert the fake hub's revert requests in order; assert count(entries of kind 'revert') == 1 and unread; one more row: the fake hub already holds reverting change 10 of change 7 -> assert the incident uses change 10 and one revert request was sent
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN the hub answers a revert with the reverting change, or names it in `409 already_reverted`, THE nightshiftd SHALL report the checks `nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review` and `nightshift-release` as `passed` on the reverting change's version with the hub client's `ReportCheck`, each with the summary `revert after failed health command on <the landed commit of the item whose landing failed>`, and then ask `land.Service.LandChange(ctx, Request{Workspace, Change, Version})` of package 07 to land that version
   → three reports with the reverting change's number, its version, the status `passed` and that summary reach the hub before the land is asked; the land request names that change and version; the summary of the repair's reverting change names the same commit; an outcome `landed` stores `LandedSHA` with the incident; an error of `LandChange` (the hub could not be asked) is returned from the step and the land is asked again at its next call
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/health/revert_test.go: the case 'the repair item landed and health fails' of the table above; assert the fake hub's checks of change 10 == {nightshift-gate, nightshift-review, nightshift-release} each 'passed' on version 1 with the summary 'revert after failed health command on ' + C; assert each report precedes lander.calls' LandChange({Workspace: 'demo', Change: 10, Version: 1}); the same for the reverting change of 7 with the same summary; LandChange returns an error once -> the step returns it, and the next call asks the same land and reports no check twice
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN package 07's `LandChange` answers the land of a reverting change with the kind `pending_approval`, THE nightshiftd SHALL open an `approval` decision for the reverting change with `land.Service.OpenApproval(ctx, ApprovalRequest{Item, Workspace, Change, Version, Requirements, Owner: "revert"})`, mark it urgent with the inbox's `SetUrgent` (new in package 03's `internal/inbox`, added by this package), so that `GET /api/v1/decisions` lists it before every open decision that is not urgent, and ask for the same land again when the function registered with `OnApprovalAnswered("revert", fn)` is called with the option `approve`
   → one `approval` decision on the thread of the item whose landing failed, answered with `urgent: true`; the open decisions are listed with the urgent ones first, oldest first among themselves, then the others oldest first; a decision opened through the inbox's `Open` with `Urgent: true` is urgent too, and one opened without it answers `urgent: false`; after `approve` the next call of the step asks `LandChange` with the same change and version and opens no second decision; `reject` and `abandon` are a refused land (REQ-3.5); the workspace stays `red` meanwhile
   Check: integration

In internal/inbox/decision_test.go and internal/inbox/routes_test.go (package 03's files): open decisions A at T1, B at T2, C at T3 with Urgent true, D at T4 then inbox.SetUrgent(ctx, D, true); assert get('/api/v1/decisions') ids == [C, D, A, B] and items[0].urgent == true and items[2].urgent == false; answer C; assert ids == [D, A, B]; in internal/cli/inbox_test.go assert the Action section prints the served order

Second case: Reopen fails once with a hub error -> the incident is not closed, and the next VerifyStep calls Reopen again and closes it. 1. [REQ-3.5] IF the health command exits with a code other than 0 or times out on the commit the last reverting change landed as, the hub refuses a revert with any answer other than `already_reverted`, `LandChange` answers the land of a reverting change with a kind other than `landed` and `pending_approval`, or the `approval` decision of a reverting change is answered `reject` or `abandon`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL leave the workspace `red` and the item `verifying`, move the incident to the phase `main_red`, and open one decision of the kind `main_red` on the item's thread, with the evidence `health command output` (the last output) and `commits tried` (every commit of the incident a health command ran on, with its result, and every refusal), whose only option is `resume`
   → the decision's `options` are exactly [`resume`], recommended, with `blocks` `workspace <slug>` and the question `Main branch of <slug> is unhealthy; resume when it is repaired?`; the workspace's state is `red`; no further repair, revert or land is asked while the decision is open; a second call of the step opens no second `main_red` decision
   Check: integration

### REQ-4: Publishing to origin

**Rationale:** The hub's branch is not where the project lives: work is done when origin has it, and origin must only ever get a branch the health command passed on.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of an item in `publishing` whose workspace is `green`, with no item of the workspace in `verifying` and no health run on a fast-forwarded tip pending, and the hub answers `POST …/branches/{default branch}/push` with the result `pushed` or `up_to_date`, THE nightshiftd SHALL append the entry `push` to the item's thread, move the item to `done`, and append the entry `published` with the text `change <n> is on origin as <commit>; <N> tokens spent`, marking the thread unread, where the commit is the change's landed commit and N the sum of the input, cache-creation and output tokens of every session of the item
   → one push request, with the worker token and no `force`; the item is `done`; the thread is unread and holds `push of <branch> to origin: <result>` and the `published` entry; the hub saw no request that deletes, extends or otherwise changes the item's fork
   Check: integration
   - setup: a publish service over a copy of the store template with the real item service, inbox and session table, the fake hub extended with a scriptable push route and an origin head per workspace, item 12 in `publishing` with change 7 landed as C and two sessions of 1,200 and 300 counted tokens
   ```
   new file internal/publish/push_test.go, fixtures in internal/publish/helpers_test.go, a table over the fake hub's push result {'pushed', 'up_to_date'}: err = svc.PublishStep(ctx, item12); assert err == nil; assert the fake hub's push requests == [('demo', 'main', no force)]; assert items.Get(12).State == 'done'; assert entries hold {kind: 'push', text: 'push of main to origin: ' + result} and {kind: 'published', text: 'change 7 is on origin as ' + C + '; 1500 tokens spent'}; assert the thread is unread; assert the fake hub saw no request for the fork 'demo--i12'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the hub answers the push with `409 non_fast_forward`, THE nightshiftd SHALL sync the workspace from origin once through `land.Service.SyncOrigin` of package 07, handle the default branch's result as REQ-5 says, and, where that lets work go on, ask the push once more in the same call of the step
   → the hub sees a push, a sync and at most one more push in that order; a second `non_fast_forward` leaves the item `publishing` and the workspace `green`, opens no decision and is not counted as a failure; the next call of the step starts again with a push
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/publish/push_test.go, a table over {push 409 non_fast_forward, sync 'up_to_date', push 'pushed' -> item done and requests [push, sync, push]; push 409, sync 'ahead', push 409 again -> item 'publishing', workspace 'green', no decision, requests [push, sync, push]; push 409, sync 'diverged' -> requests [push, sync], workspace 'held' as REQ-5.4 says}: svc.PublishStep(ctx, item12); assert the fake hub's request log and the states
   ```

[REQ-4.3] IF the hub answers the push with `422 origin_rejected`, `502 origin_unauthenticated`, `502 origin_forbidden`, `502 origin_not_found`, or with any error answer other than `non_fast_forward`, `origin_unreachable`, `upstream_error` and `origin_timeout`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL set the workspace's state to `held`, call `Notify` with the event `workspace_held`, open a decision of the kind `origin` on the thread of the item whose push it was, with the hub's error type and message as the reason, whose only option is `retry`, and leave the item `publishing`
   → the workspace's state is `held`; the decision's `options` are exactly [`retry`], recommended, its question is `Origin refused the push of <branch> of <slug>: <message>; retry?`, its evidence `reason` holds `<error_type>: <message>` and `blocks` is `workspace <slug>`; one notification with `event: workspace_held`, the workspace, the item and the thread's path; the item is `publishing`; where the workspace has an open `origin` decision already, no second one is opened

### REQ-5: The results of a sync from origin

**Rationale:** Origin moves without nightshift: what it brings in may be broken, and what it holds may contradict what the hub landed.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a sync of a workspace, run by package 07 before a landing and handed to the function this package registers with `land.Service.OnSyncResult`, or run by this package through `land.Service.SyncOrigin`, reports the default branch as `up_to_date`, `ahead` or `created`, THE nightshiftd SHALL change nothing and let the caller go on
   → `HandleSync` returns nil; the workspace's state, its threads and the store are unchanged; no health command runs
   Check: unit
   - setup: a publish service with a stub of the health service's tip check

1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN a sync reports the default branch as `fast_forward`, THE nightshiftd SHALL store that the new tip (`local_sha`) awaits its health command, run the health command on that commit through `RunHealth` with a tail of 200 lines before returning, and, when it exits 0 within the health timeout, remove the stored mark, append the entry `health` to the workspace's thread and let the caller go on
   → `HandleSync` returns nil only after the command passed; `RunHealth` was called with the slug, `local_sha` and 200; while the mark is stored no push is sent for the workspace (REQ-4.5); a mark found in the store at the start of nightshiftd is run again before any push or landing of that workspace goes on
   Check: integration

Second case: cancel the context while the command runs, reopen the store, call health.Recover(ctx); assert RunHealth is called for T again

[REQ-5.3] IF the health command exits with a code other than 0 or times out on a fast-forwarded tip, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL set the workspace's state to `red`, call `Notify` with the event `workspace_red` and no item, store an incident without an item in the phase `main_red`, open a decision of the kind `main_red` on the workspace's thread with the output and the tip as the commit tried, create no repair item and ask for no revert, and return an error to the caller

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A healthy landing is published

1. **hub** has landed the change of item 12 on the default branch of workspace `demo`, as commit C
2. **nightshiftd** calls the step of item 12, in `verifying`, brings the workspace's clone to C and runs the health command as the session user
3. **nightshiftd** reads exit code 0, moves the item to `publishing` and asks the hub to push the default branch
4. **hub** pushes the branch and answers `pushed`
5. **origin** holds C as the head of its default branch
6. **nightshiftd** moves the item to `done` and writes the `published` entry, which marks the thread unread
7. **person** runs `nightshift inbox --unread` and `nightshift thread show <id>` and reads the change, the commit and the tokens spent

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with internal/health and internal/publish registered as the steps of `verifying` and `publishing` with the scheduler of package 04, package 02's workspace.Service with RunHealth, the command runner and gitclone, internal/item and internal/inbox on the store on disk, the hub client against the fake hub's change, push and git routes, the nightshift client's run function, git and sh as installed

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) with workspace `demo`, its repository and an origin head per workspace
- workspace `demo` registered with the health command `git rev-parse HEAD > "$OUT"`
- item 12 walked to `verifying` by the e2e helper, with change 7 landed as C on the fake hub and one session of 1,500 tokens in the session table
- sessions unisolated

**End state:**

- `nightshift item show 12` prints `state: done`
- the file `$OUT` holds C
- the fake hub's origin head of `demo` is C and it saw exactly one push request
- `nightshift inbox --unread` lists the item's thread, and `nightshift thread show` prints the entries `health`, `push` and `published` with `change 7 is on origin as <C>; 1500 tokens spent`
- `nightshift workspace show demo` prints `demo: green`

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go (package 01's file, with its startDaemon helper): d = startDaemon(cfg unisolated); register demo; seedLanded(d, item 12, change 7, C); eventually cli item show 12 contains 'state: done'; assert read($OUT) == C; assert fakeHub.OriginHead('demo') == C; assert len(fakeHub.Pushes('demo')) == 1; assert cli inbox --unread lists the thread; assert cli thread show contains 'change 7 is on origin as ' + C + '; 1500 tokens spent'
```

### PATH-2: A landing that breaks the main branch is repaired once and then reverted

1. **nightshiftd** runs the health command on the landed commit of item 12; it exits 1
2. **nightshiftd** sets workspace `demo` `red`, runs the notification command with `workspace_red`, and creates the repair item 13 with item 12's package, the repair class, the repair mark and the health command's output as a finding
3. **implementer** works in item 13's new fork as a rework with that finding and pushes a change that does not remove the cause
4. **reviewer** agrees with the repair's change
5. **hub** lands the repair's change although the workspace is `red`
6. **nightshiftd** runs the health command on the repair's landed commit; it exits 1 again
7. **nightshiftd** asks the hub to revert the repair's change, reports the three checks as passed on the reverting change and asks its land, then does the same for item 12's change
8. **hub** opens and lands both reverting changes
9. **nightshiftd** runs the health command on the last revert's commit; it exits 0; sets the workspace `green`, abandons item 13 and has item 12 moved to `awaiting_approval` with its `plan` decision opened with the failure's output
10. **person** runs `nightshift inbox --action` and `nightshift decision show <id>` and reads the health command's output

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with internal/health and internal/publish and, as daemon.Run wires them, package 05's change and plan services, package 06's implementing, gate and review steps with Rework, SetClass and UsePackageOf, and package 07's landing step with SetRepair and LandChange, package 04's scheduler and session service with the fake `claude` executable and agentkit-go's provider/faux, package 02's workspace.Service, command runner and gitclone, the hub client against the fake hub's revert, check, land, sync, push and git routes, a real notification command (a shell script), the nightshift client's run function

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub with workspace `demo`, whose repository holds the finished package of item 12 that package 05 planned and kept, and with the revert route
- the health command `test ! -f BROKEN`, and item 12's landed change adding the file `BROKEN`
- the fake `claude` script commits a file other than `BROKEN` and pushes; the fake `speca` of package 06 passes the gate; the faux provider answers the verdict `agree`
- item 12 walked to `verifying` by the e2e helper; sessions unisolated

**End state:**

- the fake hub holds the repair's change and two reverting changes, all landed, each reverting change with the three checks `passed` and the summary `revert after failed health command on <C>`
- `nightshift workspace show demo` prints `demo: green`
- `nightshift item show 12` prints `state: awaiting_approval` and `waiting on: plan decision <id>`, and `nightshift item show 13` prints `state: abandoned` and `parent: item 12`
- `nightshift decision show <id>` prints an evidence line `health command output`
- the item's thread holds one `repair` entry and one `revert` entry
- the notification script's file holds one document with `event: workspace_red` and `item: 12`
- the fake hub saw no push request while the workspace was `red`, and its one implementer session of item 13 was started although the workspace's daily limit was set to 1 token

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg with [notify].command, the fake claude and the fake speca); register demo with health 'test ! -f BROKEN' and --daily-tokens 1; seedLanded(d, item 12, change 7 adding BROKEN); eventually cli item show 12 contains 'state: awaiting_approval'; assert fakeHub.Changes('demo') holds 3 landed changes after 7, two with reverts set; assert their checks and summaries; assert cli workspace show contains 'demo: green'; assert cli item show 13 contains 'state: abandoned'; id = the plan decision of cli inbox --action; assert cli decision show id contains 'evidence: health command output'; assert count of 'repair' and 'revert' entries in item 12's thread == 1 each; assert the script's file; assert fakeHub.Pushes('demo') is empty
```

### PATH-3: Origin refuses a push, and the person retries

1. **nightshiftd** asks the hub to push the default branch of `demo` for item 14, which is `publishing`
2. **origin** refuses the update by a branch rule
3. **hub** answers `422 origin_rejected` with origin's reason
4. **nightshiftd** sets the workspace `held`, runs the notification command with `workspace_held` and opens an `origin` decision on the item's thread
5. **person** reads the reason with `nightshift decision show <id>`, lifts the branch rule on the forge and runs `nightshift decide <id> --option retry`
6. **nightshift** sends the answer to `POST /api/v1/decisions/<id>/answer`
7. **nightshiftd** syncs the workspace, reads `ahead`, pushes, reads `pushed`, sets the workspace `green`, and at the item's next step moves it to `done`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with internal/publish and internal/health, package 07's SyncOrigin, the inbox's answer dispatch and the scheduler, the hub client against the fake hub's push and sync routes, a real notification command (a shell script), the nightshift client's run function

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub whose push route for `demo` answers 422 origin_rejected `protected branch hook declined` until the test lifts it
- item 14 walked to `publishing` by the e2e helper, with its change landed

**End state:**

- before the answer: `nightshift workspace show demo` prints `demo: held`, `nightshift inbox --action` lists one `origin` decision, `nightshift decision show` prints the reason and the one option `retry`, and the script's file holds one document with `event: workspace_held`
- within 5 seconds of `nightshift decide` exiting 0: `nightshift workspace show demo` prints `demo: green` and `nightshift item show 14` prints `state: done`
- the fake hub saw the requests push, sync, push, push in that order, the last answered `up_to_date`
- no `origin` decision is open

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg with [notify].command); fakeHub.RefusePush('demo', 422, 'origin_rejected', 'protected branch hook declined'); seedLanded and walk item 14 to 'publishing'; eventually cli workspace show contains 'demo: held'; id = the origin decision of cli inbox --action; assert cli decision show id contains 'protected branch hook declined' and 'option retry'; fakeHub.AllowPush('demo'); assert cli.Run(['decide', id, '--option', 'retry']) == 0; eventually cli item show 14 contains 'state: done'; assert cli workspace show contains 'demo: green'; assert fakeHub.Requests('push','sync') == [push, sync, push, push]
```

## External APIs

### `Parley REST API (agent-fox-dev/parley, docs/api.md)` (commit 7eabfb9) — verified

| Symbol | Import Path | Signature | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/revert` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/revert` | `scope changes:write; the owner of {slug}; optional body {title, intent, draft, auto_land, session_id}; 201 with the new change {number, version, state, reverts, …}, opened from the branch revert/<number> into the original's target; 409 change_not_landed; 409 already_reverted with error.details.reverted_by; 400 nothing_to_land; 409 revert_conflict with error.details.conflict; 400 target_not_found; a refusal leaves no branch and no change` |  |
| `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}` | `scope changes:read; 200 the change {number, state: draft\|open\|landed\|abandoned, version, head_sha, landed: null \| {sha, at, by, land_id, commits}, reverts, reverted_by, …}` |  |
| `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` | `scope checks:write; body {status: pending\|passed\|failed, version, summary (at most 2,000 characters), url, details}; 200 with the check; one result per version and name, a report replaces the earlier one whole` |  |
| `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/land` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/land` | `scope changes:write; optional body {expected_version, stack, override, session_id}; query wait 0..60; 200 the attempt with status landed and landed_sha; 202 still running; 409 land_conflict; 409 policy_blocked with blocked.status pending\|blocked and blocked.requirements; 409 version_mismatch; 503 land_failed; the attempt in error.details` |  |

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/health/... ./internal/publish/... ./internal/inbox/... ./internal/hub/... ./internal/hubtest/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/daemon/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `01` — uses the store and its migrations, the hub client with its typed error and `Available`, the fake hub `internal/hubtest` and the e2e helper, and adds the revert and the push to the hub client
- `02` — runs the health command through `workspace.Service.RunHealth`, sets `red`, `held` and `green` with `SetState`, and syncs through the hub client's `Sync`
- `03` — moves items with `Transition`, writes thread entries with `Append`, declares the kinds `main_red` and `origin` and their handlers in the inbox's registry, adds `urgent` to its decisions, and calls `Notify`
- `04` — registers the steps of `verifying` and `publishing` with `Scheduler.RegisterStep`, asks for repairs in `sched.ClassRepair`, uses `Paused`, `OnResume` and `Wake`, and reads an item's tokens from the session table
- `05` — reads the item's change with `change.Service.Get` and has the item's `plan` decision opened again with `plan.Service.Reopen` and the failure's output
- `06` — runs a repair as an item through `Rework` and `SetClass` of `internal/impl`, adds `UsePackageOf` to it, and reports the three checks on a reverting change with the hub client's `ReportCheck`
- `07` — marks the repair item with `SetRepair`, lands reverting changes with `LandChange`, asks for their approval with `OpenApproval` and `OnApprovalAnswered`, registers `HandleSync` with `OnSyncResult` and syncs with `SyncOrigin`

- 3.5 For each reverting change call the hub client's ReportCheck three times (`nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review`, `nightshift-release`) with the status `passed`, the change's version and the summary `revert after failed health command on <the landed commit of the item whose landing failed>`, then package 07's LandChange with the workspace, the change and the version; store `LandedSHA` of an outcome `landed`; return an error of LandChange from the step

- 3.7 On the outcome `pending_approval` call package 07's OpenApproval with the item whose landing failed, the reverting change, its version, the outcome's requirements and the owner `revert`, mark the decision with SetUrgent and store its id; register with OnApprovalAnswered for the owner `revert` a function that stores the option with the incident and wakes the scheduler: after `approve` the step asks the same land again

### 4. Push the default branch to origin and finish the item (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the behaviours to internal/publish/push_test.go and confirm they fail; keep the fixtures in internal/publish/helpers_test.go: a publish service over a copy of the store template with the real item service, inbox and session table, a recording stub of the workspace functions, a stub of the health service's TipPending and VerifyTip, a recording notifier and an injected clock
- 4.2 Add `Push(ctx, slug, branch)` to the hub client of internal/hub, sent with the worker credential and without `force`, answering `{branch, sha, result}` or the typed error; add to internal/hubtest a push route with an origin head per workspace (a push moves it to the hub's head) and scriptable answers, and a request log tests read
- 4.3 Add internal/publish with a store migration: per workspace the count of failed pushes in a row with the time of the next try, and the same for syncs; construct the service with publish.New from interfaces as internal/health does, with the interval (default 1 minute) and the number of further tries (default 5) as parameters
- 4.4 Add to the session service of internal/session a read of an item's tokens: the sum of the input, cache-creation and output tokens of every session of the item in the session table
- 4.5 Add Service.PublishStep(ctx, item), the step function of `publishing`: return nil without a request while the workspace is `red` or `held`, an item of it is `verifying`, the health service reports a pending tip, the hub is not available to the worker token, or the time of the next try has not come
- 4.6 Otherwise push the workspace's default branch (from the hub client's Workspace); on `pushed` or `up_to_date` set the count to zero, append `push`, move the item to `done` and append `published` with the change's number, its `landed.sha` and the item's tokens, with the unread mark; send nothing about the fork

Add the function that holds a workspace: SetState `held`, Notify `workspace_held`, Open an `origin` decision on the given thread with the question, the evidence and `blocks`, and nothing at all when the workspace has an open `origin` decision already
- 4.9 Hold the workspace, with the decision on the item's thread, for every error answer of the push other than `non_fast_forward`, `origin_unreachable`, `upstream_error` and `origin_timeout`
- 4.10 For those three: add one to the count and store the time of the next try; at the sixth in a row hold the workspace with that error as the reason and set the count to zero

### 5. Handle every result of a sync from origin (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the behaviours to internal/publish/sync_test.go and confirm they fail; make the sync route of internal/hubtest scriptable where it is not: the result, `local_sha` and `origin_sha` of the default branch, a missing branch, and an error answer
- 5.2 Add Service.HandleSync(ctx, r), where r is package 07's land.SyncResult{Workspace, Branch, Result, LocalSHA, OriginSHA, Err}, and Service.Sync(ctx, slug), which calls package 07's land.Service.SyncOrigin and hands its result, or its error as Err, to HandleSync
- 5.3 Return nil and change nothing for `up_to_date`, `ahead` and `created`
- 5.4 Add to internal/health Service.VerifyTip(ctx, slug, commit), TipPending(slug) and Recover(ctx): VerifyTip stores the tip as pending, runs RunHealth on it with a tail of 200 lines, and on exit code 0 in time removes the mark and appends `health` to the thread WorkspaceThread gives; Recover, called in daemon.Run before the scheduler starts, runs VerifyTip for every mark left in the store
- 5.5 On another exit code or the timeout VerifyTip sets the workspace `red`, notifies `workspace_red` without an item, stores an incident without an item in the phase `main_red`, opens the `main_red` decision on the workspace's thread with the output and the tip, removes the mark and returns an error; it creates no repair item and asks for no revert
- 5.6 For `fast_forward` HandleSync calls VerifyTip with `local_sha` and returns what it returns
- 5.7 For `diverged` hold the workspace through the function of the task before, with the decision on the workspace's thread, the question the criterion gives and the evidence `hub head` and `origin head`, and return an error
- 5.8 For a failed sync (Err set, the result `reset` or `name_conflict`, or no entry for the default branch) return an error with the reason; when no try is pending for the workspace, add one to the count and start a timer for the interval that calls Sync again (package 07 itself does not sync a workspace again for 1 minute after a sync that did not pass); ignore a failure handed over while a try is pending; at the sixth failure in a row hold the workspace with the reason, the decision on the workspace's thread, and set the count to zero; a try that succeeds sets it to zero
- 5.9 Stop the timers in a named shutdown step of package 01, and at start begin a try for every workspace whose stored count is above zero
- 5.10 Register HandleSync with package 07's `land.Service.OnSyncResult` in daemon.Run
- 5.11 Add HandleSync, Sync, VerifyTip and the hook to docs/architecture.md

### 6. Carry out the answers `resume` and `retry`, and prove the flows end to end (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the behaviours to internal/health/mainred_test.go and internal/publish/decision_test.go and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Add health.Service.Resume and register it with the inbox's OnAnswer for `main_red` and `resume`: read `head_sha` with the hub client's Workspace and run RunHealth on it with a tail of 200 lines; a hub or command error is returned, so that the inbox calls the handler again
- 6.3 On exit code 0 in time: SetState `green`, close the incident, append `health` and `workspace_green` to the decision's thread; for an incident with an item, read whether the reverting change of the item's change has landed and call plan.Service.Reopen as after a revert, or move the item to `publishing`; a repair item still `verifying` is abandoned as after a revert where its change's revert has landed and moved to `publishing` where it has not, and its repair mark is removed
- 6.4 On another exit code or the timeout: add the commit and its result to the incident's commits tried and open a new `main_red` decision on the same thread with the new output, storing its id with the incident
- 6.5 Add publish.Service.Retry and register it with OnAnswer for `origin` and `retry`: call package 07's SyncOrigin and judge the default branch's result without the timed tries (pass `up_to_date`, `ahead`, `created` and a `fast_forward` whose VerifyTip returned nil), then push the default branch once
- 6.6 When both succeeded: SetState `green`, append `push` and `workspace_green` to the decision's thread, set both counts to zero and call the scheduler's Wake.
